title: A wall-clock stop throws away the attempt's uncommitted work
description:
From the Phase 3 run (epic-9pd, tick 0z0 attempt 1), 2026-09-15.

The worker spent 40 minutes misdiagnosing a one-token import typo while holding real, uncommitted implementation: a new internal/cli/watch.go, held-attempt tests, and changes to dispatch.go and settle.go. It had committed nothing. Had the one-hour wall clock fired, the attempt would have settled with no commits, been rejected as no-commits, and a fresh attempt would have started from nothing — every line of that work gone. It survived only because an operator pointed the worker at the typo with 17 minutes left.

The wall clock is the only mechanical bound on a worker that is alive but lost, so what it does to the work is what the bound costs.

Wanted: when the wall clock stops an attempt, snapshot its working tree before teardown — tracked changes and untracked files, excluding the report and build output — onto a ref of its own (for example refs/ticfac/wip/<run>/<tick>/<attempt>) or into the attempt's state directory, and record where. The snapshot is NOT merged and is NOT evidence of completion; it is material the next attempt can be pointed at (see nvn).

Care: the boundary exclusions still apply to a snapshot; nothing under .tick/ or .ticfac/ may ride along, and the report is archived separately (35h).
acceptance_criteria: An attempt stopped at its wall clock with uncommitted changes leaves them recoverable at a recorded location, never merged; a test stops an attempt holding an uncommitted file and asserts the file is recoverable after teardown and the attempt is still not ready-to-merge
